causes.label: network_outage
causes.quote: At 1.24 pm, due to extreme localised storm conditions, the Heywood interconnector which links Victoria and South Australia failed. Six high voltage transmission towers in between Lismore and Moorabool in Victoria collapsed resulting in South Australia being electrically isolated from the rest of the market.

causes.label: wind_output
causes.quote: Constraints invoked to maintain the system in a secure state: • limited cheaper priced generation at Lake Bonney wind farms 2 and 3 • limited cheaper priced generation at the Snowtown north and south wind farms.

causes.label: solar_output
causes.quote: limited the amount of generation unable to provide other services, such as solar and wind, in the region to less than 1300 MW

causes.label: fcas_co_optimisation
causes.quote: Due to the separation event, South Australia needed to source FCAS locally... The trade-off between energy and FCAS meant that not all cheaply priced generation in the region could be used to meet the demand for energy. This contributed to the amount of energy constrained as shown in Figure 2.

causes.label: unscheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: Within the 2 pm trading interval a small number of generation units experienced technical issues with their plant and adjusted the amount of generation available to the market... Overall while the amount of MW removed was only small (around 150 MW), it was a factor that contributed to the high price outcomes.

causes.label: demand
causes.quote: Demand was up slightly on earlier forecasts and generator availability slightly lower.

interconnectors_named.name: Heywood interconnector
interconnectors_named.quote: At 1.24 pm, due to extreme localised storm conditions, the Heywood interconnector which links Victoria and South Australia failed.

interconnectors_named.name: MurrayLink interconnector
interconnectors_named.quote: This saw a decrease of 35 MW of imports from Victoria across the Heywood interconnector, however this was more than offset by an increase of 84 MW of imports across the MurrayLink interconnector.

intervals.quote: The spot price for the 2 pm trading interval in South Australia reached $9832/MWh.

network_outages.quote: At 1.24 pm, due to extreme localised storm conditions, the Heywood interconnector which links Victoria and South Australia failed. Six high voltage transmission towers in between Lismore and Moorabool in Victoria collapsed resulting in South Australia being electrically isolated from the rest of the market.

peak_price.quote: The spot price for the 2 pm trading interval in South Australia reached $9832/MWh.

rebid_set_price.quote: Overall rebidding from low to high prices did not contribute to the high priced trading interval in South Australia.

causes.label: demand
causes.quote: High temperatures in Victoria and New South Wales led to high demand in both regions.

causes.label: wind_output
causes.quote: Availability in these trading intervals was around 700 MW lower than forecast four hour prior, mainly due to plant issues in New South Wales and lower than forecast wind generation in Victoria.

causes.label: scheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: Of the 14,400 MW of thermal capacity registered to be available during summer, 1100 MW was not. AGL's Liddell unit 1 (450 MW) had been offline since the previous day due to a tube leak while EnergyAustralia's Mount Piper unit 2 (650 MW) had been offline since 23 January for a planned outage.

causes.label: unscheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: Snowy Hydro's Colongra power station experienced technical issues which saw its unit 2 (169 MW) fail to start after receiving a target to generate. This occurred at 2.08 pm... The unit remained offline until 3.40 pm. AGL's Liddell unit 2 and Bayswater unit 4 plants also reduced their availability due to a plant failure and milling limits respectively. These outages saw a combined 330 MW of generation capacity unavailable during the 3 pm and 3.30 pm trading intervals.

causes.label: network_outage
causes.quote: As highlighted in section 3.1, there was an unplanned outage of the Heywood interconnector. The outage resulted in no imports being available to Victoria from South Australia across Heywood during the high price periods.

causes.label: interconnector_limit
causes.quote: Victoria was not able to import any generation from South Australia and it required imports from New South Wales to meet demand, opposite from what was forecast four hours prior.

interconnectors_named.name: Heywood interconnector
interconnectors_named.quote: As highlighted in section 3.1, there was an unplanned outage of the Heywood interconnector.

interconnectors_named.name: MurrayLink interconnector
interconnectors_named.quote: South Australia is electrically connected to Victoria by the Heywood and Murray Link interconnectors.

interconnectors_named.name: Vic-NSW interconnector
interconnectors_named.quote: Table 5 shows the actual and four hour forecast flows on both the Heywood and Vic-NSW interconnectors.

intervals.quote: On 31 January 2020 the wholesale spot price for electricity exceeded $5000/MWh for the 2 pm trading interval in South Australia and multiple times in Victoria and New South Wales from 3 pm to 7 pm.

network_outages.quote: As highlighted in section 3.1, there was an unplanned outage of the Heywood interconnector. The outage resulted in no imports being available to Victoria from South Australia across Heywood during the high price periods.

rebid_set_price.quote: Rebidding of capacity from low to high prices did not contribute to the price exceeding $5000/MWh in any of the high priced trading intervals on the day.
